1. Market Overview & Long-Term Price Trend

Gold has appreciated from $273.90 in August 2000 to $5377.30 by early 2025, representing a compound annual growth rate of 12.38%. The trajectory is not linear; it is characterized by multi-year bull phases, sharp corrections, and extended consolidations.

Figure 1. Gold closing price with volatility regime shading. Low-Vol (blue), High-Vol (orange), Crisis (red).

Key phases:

  • 2000–2005: Baseline accumulation; prices oscillated in a $250–$450 range with relatively muted volatility.
  • 2005–2011: Sustained bull market driven by USD weakness and post-crisis monetary expansion. Peak near $1,900 in September 2011.
  • 2011–2015: Protracted bear market / consolidation; prices retraced ~45% from peak to trough.
  • 2016–2019: Recovery and range-bound behavior ($1,050–$1,550).
  • 2020–2025: New all-time highs amid pandemic-driven monetary stimulus and subsequent inflation hedging. Prices breached $2,700.
Figure 2. Peak-to-trough drawdown over the full sample. The deepest sustained drawdown occurred during 2011–2015.

2. Volatility Analysis & Regime Detection

We define regimes using the 30-day rolling annualized volatility of daily log returns. Thresholds are set at the median (14.8%) and 90th percentile (23.4%) of the rolling series.

Figure 3. Rolling annualized volatility with regime thresholds. Crisis episodes coincide with GFC (2008), Eurozone stress (2011), COVID-19 (2020), and the 2022 rate-hike cycle.

Regime summary:

RegimeThresholdTypical Context
Low-Vol< 14.8%Trending / calm macro environment
High-Vol14.8% – 23.4%Transition periods, policy uncertainty
Crisis≥ 23.4%Systemic risk events, liquidity stress

Volatility is clustered: high-vol periods tend to follow high-vol periods, consistent with GARCH-type dynamics. The GFC and COVID shocks produced the largest volatility spikes, but the 2022–2023 rate-hike cycle also generated sustained elevated volatility without a commensurate price collapse.

4. Return Distribution & Tail Risk

Daily log returns exhibit negative skewness (-0.47) and excess kurtosis (7.02), indicating fatter tails than a normal distribution. The Jarque–Bera test strongly rejects normality (p < 0.001).

Figure 7. Histogram of daily returns with normal overlay and VaR markers.
Figure 8. Q-Q plot against normal distribution. Deviations in the tails confirm leptokurtosis.

The 1-day 99% VaR of -3.10% implies that on 1% of trading days, losses exceeded this level. CVaR (expected shortfall) is markedly worse, highlighting asymmetric tail risk.

5. Momentum Dynamics & Liquidity Behavior

We evaluate medium-term momentum via the 50/200-day moving average crossover and short-term momentum via 20-day and 60-day rate-of-change.

Figure 9. MA50/MA200 crossover for the last 5 years. Golden crosses (green dashed) and death crosses (red dashed) mark regime shifts in trend.

Over the full sample, the 50/200 crossover has captured the major directional shifts (e.g., 2018–2019 recovery, 2020 breakout, 2022 correction). However, whipsaws during choppy periods (2021, 2023) generated false signals.

Figure 10. Daily volume vs absolute return (2010–2025). Spearman ρ = 0.094 (p < 0.001). Higher volume tends to accompany larger absolute price moves, though the linear Pearson correlation is near zero due to outliers.

Liquidity notes: Volume data prior to 2004 is unreliable (frequent zeros). In the reliable period, volume spikes coincide with crisis episodes and trend accelerations. The rank correlation between volume and absolute return is 0.094, confirming that large moves are information-rich.

6. Key Takeaways & Forward-Looking Considerations

  • Long-term compounding is strong but path-dependent. Gold’s ~12.4% annualized return over 24+ years masks multi-year drawdowns exceeding 44%. Position sizing must account for drawdown tolerance.
  • Volatility regimes are identifiable and persistent. The median 30-day vol of 14.8% separates calm from turbulent periods; the 90th percentile (23.4%) flags crisis states. Regime-aware sizing can improve risk-adjusted returns.
  • Tail risk is real and non-normal. Excess kurtosis of 7.0 means extreme moves occur far more often than a normal model predicts. VaR/CVaR frameworks should use historical or fat-tailed distributions.
  • Seasonal effects are marginal. The ANOVA p-value (0.535) does not reach significance. Any month-of-year or day-of-week patterns are noisy and not actionable without additional confirmation.
  • Momentum works in trending environments. MA crossovers align with major bull/bear phases but suffer in range-bound markets. Combining momentum with volatility regime filters may reduce whipsaw risk.
  • Current context (2024–2025): Gold is near all-time highs with elevated but not crisis-level volatility. Analysts should monitor whether the next regime shift moves into High-Vol or Crisis territory—driven by geopolitical shocks, central bank policy pivots, or USD strength.
